new_statements.quote: Stress, that is the prominence of one syllable as compared with neighbouring syllables by means of higher pressure of the airstream, is not contrastive in Meta'. It is, however, useful to distinguish between stressed and unstressed syllables, since certain tone rules can best be formulated by recourse to this distinction. The initial syllable of each root has phonetic stress. All affix syllables and non-initial root syllables are unstressed. In the following examples stress is marked by ['] but will generally be left unmarked outside of this subsection. (1) (a) ə̀-'bàm ~ ə̀-'bàmɨ 'bag' (b) ə-'zéd ~ ə-'zérɨ 'tree, stick' (c) 'náb 'house, family' (d) 'wə̀d 'person'
new_statements.citation: Spreda, Klaus W. 1995. Draft and notes towards a sketch grammar of Meta'. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon (MS). §2.2 Suprasegmental features, §2.2.1 Stress, section p. 1 (PDF p. 2; footer 'DR2_2.DOC 11.05.95'). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47705.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Meta' is a tone language (three register tonemes, four phonetic levels plus six contours per the same source); stress is not contrastive. Phonetic stress falls on the initial syllable of the root; noun-class prefixes and other affixes and non-initial root syllables are unstressed. The stressed syllable is where long vowels can occur (Spreda 1991, 'Long vowels in Meta'' p. 1: 'Long vowels can only occur in stressed syllables. The stressed CV-syllables are generally roots of nouns and verbs.').
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the distinction is said to be needed only for formulating certain tone rules (footnote 'See §xxx for details' — cross-reference never filled in in the draft).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: prefix + root nouns and verb roots cited in isolation (e.g. ə̀-'bàm 'bag', ə-'zéd 'tree'); the source is an unrevised 1995 SIL draft ('1st Rev'), posted 'as is'.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is for Meta' proper (Spreda's 'Meta''/'Metta', ISO mgo, glottocode meta1238). Tunviken 2013, Njeck 2008 and Casali 1995 describe Moghamo, the divergent Batibo variety that Glottolog Spreda's 1995 draft is an SIL working manuscript posted without peer review, not a published grammar.

sources.citation: Tunviken, Jonas. 2013. A phonological sketch of Moghamo, a Narrow Grassfields Bantu language. Yaoundé: SIL / CABTAL. 43 pp. SIL archive entry 53985 (SIL tags the subject language as Ngamambo [nbv]; the text itself says ISO 639-3 mgo, Moghamo of Batibo Subdivision).
sources.note: No stress section. §6 Tone p. 32: 'Moghamo makes use of both grammatical and lexical tone'; eight phonetic pitches, five tonemes /H M L HL LH/ from underlying H and L; footnote 14: 'Meta' has ten [pitches]... (Spreda 1986: 10, 14)'. Only mention of stress is methodological ('avoids possible emphatic stressing', p. 40).
